findings.title: Failed USE keyspace permanently bricks pool with no recovery path
findings.claim: PoolRefiller::use_keyspace sets current_keyspace unconditionally and never clears it on a failed USE, so every newly opened connection is now discarded and the pool loops in Broken/backoff forever, whereas before a failed USE on a fresh connection was just logged and the connection stayed usable.

findings.title: Keyspace-set failure log downgraded from warn! to debug!
findings.claim: The removed code logged the keyspace-setting failure at warn!, but the new branch logs the same message at debug!, even though the consequence is now more severe (connection dropped, pool may go Broken).

findings.title: PoolRefiller has no Drop impl, leaking total_connections metric on pool teardown
findings.claim: The PR adds metric decrements at three clear sites but there is no impl Drop for PoolRefiller and no decrement when the refiller task exits (run() returning on keyspace-channel-closed), so dropping a pool (node removal or session shutdown) leaks the full total_connections count.

findings.title: UseKeyspaceError doesn't satisfy ConnectionError's documented 'connection must be dropped' contract
findings.claim: ConnectionError's doc comment says it indicates the connection can no longer be used and should be dropped, but UseKeyspaceError::KeyspaceNameMismatch and RequestTimeout don't mean the transport is broken; flowing into ConnectionPoolError::Broken{last_connection_error} makes users see a healthy-connection error reported as a connection-level failure.

findings.title: Deferring the sharding block behind keyspace setup loses shard discovery on the USE-failure path
findings.claim: Moving the keyspace check above maybe_reshard/shard-aware-port update means a connection whose USE fails never contributes its ShardInfo, so the pool never learns sharder or shard_aware_port while keyspace setup keeps failing, compounding finding 1.

findings.title: New metrics test still wall-clock busy-polls despite its 'avoid busy-waiting' title
findings.claim: The test polls get_total_connections() in a 1ms sleep loop under a 5s tokio timeout on a real clock, making it load-sensitive on CI, even though pool_updated_notify is already wired into mock_pool_refiller but unused.

findings.title: decrement_total_connections loops instead of a single bulk atomic update
findings.claim: for _ in 0..count { self.metrics.dec_total_connections(); } performs count separate atomic operations where a dec_total_connections_by(n) method would be one operation and read better at all three call sites.

findings.title: 'Decrement then clear excess' pattern duplicated across three call sites
findings.claim: Three independent sites must remember to pair the metric decrement with clearing excess connections; a single clear_excess_connections helper would make a fourth site impossible to get wrong, especially since two sites previously omitted the decrement before this PR.

findings.title: keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill test doesn't actually test a refill
findings.claim: The refiller is never run(); the test only asserts need_filling() on a static struct, verifying the predicate rather than that a refill is actually scheduled, so the test name overstates coverage.

findings.title: Undocumented magic frame bytes in test
findings.claim: Bytes::from_static(b"\0\0\0\x03\0\x08keyspace") is a hand-encoded Result/SetKeyspace body with no comment explaining the layout (result kind 3, short length 8, name), forcing anyone changing the keyspace name to rediscover the encoding.

findings.title: Test duplicates start_simulated_node's rule-building and skips setup_tracing()
findings.claim: make_rules re-implements the OPTIONS/STARTUP rules that start_simulated_node already builds, and this is the only test in the module (along with keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill) that omits setup_tracing(), so its failures produce no log output.

findings.title: Dead argument passed to start_simulated_node in resharding test
findings.claim: start_simulated_node(initial_shard_info) is immediately followed by change_request_rules that replaces SUPPORTED with a non-sharded response, so initial_shard_info has no effect and is misleading to a reader following the reshard sequence.

findings.title: PR description's 'Fixes: #1682' is a dangling issue reference
findings.claim: gh issue view 1682 fails in dkropachev/quillstone; the referenced issue number appears to be from upstream scylla-rust-driver instead.

findings.title: No test covers pool recovery from Broken(UseKeyspaceError) back to Ready
findings.claim: No test covers that a pool which went Broken(UseKeyspaceError) flips back to Ready once a later refill's USE succeeds.

findings.title: No test covers keyspace-failure-empties-pool triggering ConnectivityChangeEvent::Lost
findings.claim: No test covers the keyspace-failure-empties-the-pool path leading to emit_events firing a Lost connectivity event; the existing test deliberately keeps one connection alive so this path is never exercised.
